Contrast compares partnered versus non-partnered movement (joint action with haptic contact) and identifies social-cognition/mentalizing regions (mPFC, TPJ, pSTS), meeting both global whole-brain criteria and the local requirement for a social-related task measuring social processing.

The contrast tests partnering versus non-partnering but does not specifically probe affiliation/attachment (e.g., cooperation vs competition or bonding measures). AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not met.

Partnered versus non-partnered contrast involves exchange of haptic cues and recruits regions for perception of dynamic social signals (pSTS, TPJ), satisfying the local criteria for social communication measures in a whole-brain group contrast.
This contrast addresses partnered interaction broadly and does not specifically measure self-perception/agency or self-knowledge in isolation; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 are not met.

The partnered > non-partnered contrast activates regions involved in perceiving others' actions and dynamic social stimuli (pSTS, TPJ), matching the criteria for perception/understanding of others in a whole-brain task contrast.

Leading is a role in joint social action; the contrast isolates leader-specific neural activity (motor planning, self-orientation) within a social interaction context and meets whole-brain group criteria and the local social-processing requirement.
Leading > Conjunction isolates leader motor/planning processes but does not specifically measure affiliation or attachment; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not met.

Leading involves signaling and coordinating with a partner (exchange of haptic cues). The contrast targets leader-related communication aspects in a whole-brain task contrast, satisfying SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2.
Leading specifically emphasizes self-orientation and self-initiated action (motor planning, SMA, CMA), matching the perception/understanding-of-self construct (agency) in a whole-brain contrast.
The Leading > Conjunction contrast highlights self-initiated motor networks rather than perception/understanding of others; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 are not specifically met.

Following is an externally-oriented role within joint action; the contrast reveals sensory/social-motion and social-cognition regions (S2, pSTS, MT+/V5, vACC), meeting whole-brain and local social-processing criteria.

Following > Conjunction indexes sensory and motion-tracking networks for responsiveness to a partner, not measures of affiliation/attachment; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not met.

Following entails reception of haptic signals and perception of a partner's movement (receptive aspect of social communication); the contrast is a whole-brain task contrast that satisfies SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2.
Following is externally-driven and the contrast emphasizes sensory receptivity rather than self-awareness/agency; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 are not met.
Following engages networks for action perception and social-motion processing (pSTS, aIPL, MT+/V5), directly mapping onto perception/understanding of others in a whole-brain contrast.

Mutual condition is a symmetric social interaction and selectively recruits mentalizing and reward networks (mPFC, TPJ, PCC, nucleus accumbens), meeting whole-brain criteria and the local social-processing requirement.

Mutual > Conjunction shows activation of reward/affect centers (nucleus accumbens, amygdala) and increased mentalizing in a cooperative/reciprocal interaction, matching local criteria for affiliation/attachment-related processes.

Mutual interaction involves reciprocal exchange and mentalizing about partner intentions, engaging social-perception and communication-related regions (TPJ, pSTS), satisfying SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2.

The Mutual condition preferentially recruited mPFC and PCC, and the authors interpreted PCC involvement as self-related processing (balancing internal/external focus), meeting the local perception-self criteria in a whole-brain contrast.
Mutual > Conjunction engages mentalizing areas (TPJ, mPFC, pSTS) involved in understanding others' intentions, satisfying perception-of-others inclusion criteria in a whole-brain group contrast.

The improvisation contrast primarily probes motor-planning and working-memory networks for generation of variable movement (Leading + Solo > Mutual + Alone) rather than a task specifically designed to measure social processing; SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I1 and SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2 are not clearly met.
Improvisation contrast targets motor generation and sequence variability, not measures of affiliation/attachment; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not met.
The improvisation contrast isolates generative motor and working-memory processes rather than receptive/expressive social communication per se; SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2 are not met.

Although improvisation involves self-generated movement, the contrast was designed to identify motor-planning and working-memory networks rather than explicit self-perception/agency judgments; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 are not specifically met.
Improvisation contrast contrasts generative versus fixed movement and does not target perception/understanding of others; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 are not met.

The self-initiation contrast (self-initiated movements vs Following) is framed within the joint-action context and identifies networks (DLPFC, SPL) related to internally-driven action in social tasks, meeting whole-brain and social-processing criteria.
Self-initiation contrast isolates agency-related networks and does not specifically probe affiliation/attachment constructs; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not met.
This contrast contrasts internally- vs externally-initiated movement (agency) rather than measuring social communication exchange specifically; SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2 are not met.

The contrast explicitly contrasts self-initiated versus externally-triggered movement and identifies regions associated with self-initiation/agency (DLPFC, SPL), meeting both global whole-brain and local perception-self inclusion criteria.

Although Following (the comparator) involves responding to another, the self-initiation contrast is focused on self-generated action and not directly on perception/understanding of others; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 are not met.

Leading > Solo isolates effects of partnering during improvisation (i.e., social contact) and reveals somatosensory and partnering-related activations (S1, S2, MCC), meeting whole-brain and social-processing inclusion criteria.
Leading > Solo isolates partner-contact and somatosensory effects rather than explicit affiliation/attachment constructs; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not met.

The contrast targets partner-related signaling/interaction differences (leading with partner vs solo), implicating social-exchange processes (haptic communication) consistent with SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2 in a whole-brain contrast.

Leading > Solo highlights somatosensory and partnering-related regions (S1/S2) due to partner contact rather than directly probing self-perception/agency; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 are not specifically met.

This contrast isolates the effect of partnering during improvisation (leading with partner vs solo) and highlights somatosensory/contact effects rather than explicit perception/understanding of others' mental states; PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 are not clearly met.

Contrast indexes participants' self-related responses to being excluded (need-satisfaction/mood), meeting perception-of-self criteria in a whole-brain healthy sample.

Task is a social attribution task (internal vs external attributions) in healthy adults and the contrast is a group-level whole-brain voxelwise map measuring social processing.

Although stimuli involve friend-related scenarios, the contrast tests attribution (self vs other) rather than a measure specifically targeting affiliation/attachment; local inclusion criteria not met (AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
The task is not a social communication/production or reception task (e.g., facial/gesture communication); local inclusion criteria SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2 are not met.
Internal > external directly indexes self-responsibility/agency (perception of self) in a whole-brain group contrast on healthy adults.
This contrast emphasizes internal (self) attributions rather than perception/understanding of others; local inclusion criteria PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 are not met.
External > internal is a group-level whole-brain contrast from a social attribution task in healthy adults and measures social processing related to attributing events to others/situations.
The contrast tests attribution to others/situations rather than affiliation/attachment specifically; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not met.
This is not a communication-focused task/contrast (e.g., facial expression or communicative behavior); SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2 are not met.
The contrast emphasizes external/other attributions rather than perception/understanding of the self; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 are not met.
External > internal directly indexes attribution to others/situations and therefore measures perception/understanding of others in a whole-brain group contrast on healthy adults.

Self-serving bias contrast combines internal attributions for positive events and external attributions for negative events in a social task; it is a whole-brain group contrast measuring social processing.
The contrast indexes a motivational attributional bias rather than affiliation/attachment per se; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not met.
Self-serving bias contrast does not target communication reception/production processes; SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2 are not met.
The self-serving bias contrast includes internal attributions of positive events (self-responsibility), so it indexes perception/understanding of self in a whole-brain group-level map.

The self-serving bias contrast also combines external attributions of negative events (attributing to others/situations), thus engaging perception/understanding of others in a whole-brain group contrast.
Non-self-serving bias contrast (internal negative + external positive) is derived from the social attribution task and is a whole-brain group contrast measuring social processing.
This contrast reflects attributional style (non-self-serving) rather than a measure specifically of affiliation/attachment; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not met.
Non-self-serving bias does not target communication processes (facial/gesture/gaze exchange); SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2 are not met.

Although the contrast includes internal attributions of negative events, the contrast is constructed to capture non-self-serving attributional bias rather than a direct measure of self-perception; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 are not met for this contrast.

Non-self-serving bias includes external attributions of positive events (attributing positive events to others/situations), which indexes perception/understanding of others in a whole-brain group contrast.

Analysis models interns' intentions to recommend and relates neural responses during encoding to downstream social propagation; task is social and results are whole-brain group-level, satisfying global and local social-processing criteria.

Salesperson effect indexes social-influence ability (interns' success at persuading producers) and is a whole-brain group-level analysis; task and outcome are social in nature.

Salesperson effect is associated with bilateral TPJ, a core region for understanding others' mental states; whole-brain group-level evidence supports inclusion under perception-of-others criteria.

Buzz effect reflects outcomes of communicative processes (ideas that ‘buzzed’ and were propagated) and recruits mentalizing regions implicated in preparing messages for others; meets social-communication criteria at the whole-brain group level.

Contrast examines competition (social interaction) vs independent play in healthy adults using group-level whole-brain univariate fMRI — meets global criteria and specifically measures social processing (competition/interaction).

Stories (collapsed across content) include social-related tasks (social contracts, precautions, descriptives) and engage social cognitive systems during interpretation; meets global criteria and local criterion that a social-related task was performed.

The contrast does not target affiliation/attachment processes or contrasts (no measures of close relationships, cooperation vs stranger, etc.). Missing inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

The Stories>Rest contrast is not a Social Communication task/contrast (no explicit reception/production of communicative signals vs control). Missing inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
The contrast does not probe self-perception or self-referential judgments. Missing inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Although stories include social content, the Stories>Rest contrast is not specific to representing others' mental states (ToM) — the ToM-sensitive contrasts were the social-contract specific story contrasts. Missing inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.

Rest>Stories reflects greater activity at rest (deactivations during stories) and does not measure social processing per se. Missing inclusion criterion SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2 (analysis must measure Social Processing).

Cards>Rest collapses across Wason tasks (social contract, precaution, descriptive) and involves decisions about social scenarios (detecting violations); meets global criteria and is a social-related task.

Global criteria met (healthy adult sample; group-level whole-brain task contrasts). This contrast is a task-evoked, whole-brain comparison of cooperation with human vs. computer partners in the Prisoner’s Dilemma, directly measuring social processing (social interaction, prosocial decision-making).
Global criteria met. The contrast directly measures cooperation (a prototypical affiliation/attachment-related behavior) in a social context (human vs computer opponents).

Global criteria met. The PD cooperation contrast involves social interaction and exchange in a competitive/cooperative context (examples listed in local criteria), satisfying social communication inclusion criteria.

Global criteria met. Making cooperative/defective choices in PD involves self-referential decision processes and self-monitoring in a social decision context (fits local examples: cooperation/competition, social comparison).

Global criteria met. The contrast assesses participants’ decisions against human vs computer partners, implicating representation and reasoning about others’ behavior (theory of mind, social distance), matching perception-of-others criteria.
Global criteria met. WG>PD is a whole-brain task contrast comparing two social economic games (both involve social decision-making and prosocial/fairness processes), so it measures social processing.
Global criteria met. Welfare Game involves egalitarian choices and cooperative considerations (affiliation/attachment-related behaviors), satisfying the local criteria.

Global criteria met. Both WG and PD are social decision tasks (cooperation/competition, social comparison) included by the local social communication criteria, so the contrast measures social communication-related processes.

Global criteria met. Contrasting WG and PD involves self-relevant decision-making (choices about own payoff and fairness), in line with local perception-self examples (cooperation/competition, social comparison).
Global criteria met. WG vs PD requires reasoning about others’ strategies and potential outcomes (theory of mind/understanding others), matching local perception-of-others criteria.
Global criteria met. PD>WG is a whole-brain contrast between two social economic games; both involve social decision processes, so this contrast measures social processing.
Global criteria met. PD involves cooperation/defection decisions (affiliation/attachment domain); the contrast probes affiliation-related processes.
Global criteria met. The contrast contrasts two cooperative/competitive game contexts and thus engages social communication constructs listed in the local criteria.
Global criteria met. PD decisions are self-referential choices about one’s own payoff in social settings, meeting perception-self inclusion examples.
Global criteria met. PD requires anticipating/representing opponents’ actions (understanding others), consistent with perception-of-others inclusion criteria.
Global criteria met. This analysis examines sociality conditions within PD (human vs computer or acquaintance vs random), a direct test of social processing in decision-making contexts.
Global criteria met. The contrast evaluates cooperation under different sociality levels, directly indexing affiliation/attachment-related behavior.
Global criteria met. The sociality manipulation and PD choices reflect interactive social decision processes (cooperation/competition) covered by social communication local criteria.
Global criteria met. Varying sociality likely alters self-related valuation and monitoring during choices (self-referential decision processes), matching perception-self criteria.
Global criteria met. The contrast probes how participants represent and respond to others (human vs computer/acquaintance vs random), meeting perception-of-others inclusion criteria.
Global criteria met. High>Low sociality is a whole-brain contrast that isolates neural correlates of increased sociality during economic games — a clear social processing measure.
Global criteria met. The contrast captures increased prosocial/affiliative behavior and group-based bonding induced by the high sociality manipulation, fitting affiliation/attachment criteria.
Global criteria met. The High vs Low sociality contrast reflects differences in interactive social decision processes (cooperation, social comparison), consistent with social communication inclusion.
Global criteria met. High sociality manipulation changes self-relevant valuation and choices (self-monitoring and self-related decision processes), matching perception-self inclusion examples.
Global criteria met. The contrast explicitly tests altered representations of others under high vs low sociality (understanding others’ behavior), satisfying perception-of-others criteria.

Global criteria met. Both PD and UG involve interactive social decision-making (cooperation, bargaining, social comparison) consistent with social communication local criteria.
Global criteria met. Contrasting PD and UG involves self-relevant choices (own payoff judgments, self-control), fitting perception-self inclusion criteria.
Global criteria met. Both games require modeling opponents and anticipating their behavior; PD>UG thus probes understanding others, meeting perception-of-others criteria.
Global criteria met. UG>PD contrasts two social tasks and isolates neural activity related to bargaining/fairness processes—clearly social processing.
Global criteria met. UG involves acceptance/rejection of unfair offers and fairness norms (affiliation/attachment and social value), satisfying affiliation criteria.
Global criteria met. Ultimatum Game contrasts engage social exchange and normative communication (social comparison/cooperation), meeting social communication inclusion.
Global criteria met. UG decisions require self-referential evaluation of offers (self-related valuation and monitoring), consistent with perception-self criteria.
Global criteria met. UG requires assessing others’ intentions and fairness (theory of mind/understanding others), satisfying perception-of-others criteria.

The contrast involves exchange of socially relevant information via humor styles (production/reception of social humor), meeting social communication criteria.
Contrast focuses on self-directed humor (self-defeating vs self-enhancing), thus probes perception/understanding of the self and self-representation.

Contrast involves appreciation of socially directed humor (aggressive vs affiliative), which constitutes social communication processes (production/reception of social content).

AG and AF are other-directed humor styles; this contrast probes processing of humor targeted at others, meeting perception-of-others criteria.
AF>SE contrasts affiliative (other-directed, relationship-facilitating) vs self-enhancing humor, a social task probing social processing; global and local criteria met.
Affiliative humor (AF) specifically measures relationship-facilitating, attachment-related processes; this contrast isolates affiliative humor and therefore meets affiliation criteria.
Contrast involves affiliative humor which is a form of social communication aimed at bonding and cohesion; meets social communication criteria.
The contrast isolates affiliative (other-directed) vs self-enhancing humor and does not specifically measure perception/understanding of the self; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Affiliative humor is directed at others and probes understanding/perception of others (social intentions), satisfying perception-of-others criteria.
This main-effect contrast (other-directed > self-directed) probes social-target processing (self vs others) and meets global and local social processing criteria.
Contrast addresses target (other vs self) broadly and does not specifically measure affiliation/attachment (AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 not met).
Contrast compares processing of humor directed at others versus self, which involves aspects of social communication and perspective-taking; meets social communication criteria.
The contrast emphasizes other-directed > self-directed processing and does not isolate perception/understanding of the self (PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 not specifically met).
Other-directed > self-directed directly probes processing of stimuli about others and thus meets perception-of-others criteria.
Benign vs detrimental humor contrasts probe social motivational aspects of humor appreciation (social processing); global and local social processing criteria apply.

Contrast concerns humor motivation (benign vs detrimental) and does not specifically measure perception/understanding of the self (PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 not met).
Contrast mixes targets and motivations and does not specifically isolate perception/understanding of others (PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 not met).
Interaction between target and motivation probes combined social factors in humor appreciation (social processing); global and local social processing criteria are met.

Although the interaction may implicate relationship-facilitating humor, the interaction itself does not specifically isolate affiliation/attachment processes required by AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Interaction examines how social-target and social-motivation factors combine during humor appreciation, which involves social communication processes.
The interaction term is general and does not specifically isolate perception/understanding of the self as required by PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Contrast examines deception (simple + sophisticated) vs truth in an interactive sender-receiver game requiring Theory-of-Mind and social cognition; group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults. Meets global and local social processing criteria.
The contrast addresses deception and mentalizing in strategic interaction rather than affiliation/attachment or bond formation; does not meet AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2.

This contrast tests deception/conflict and monitoring rather than affiliation or bonding; does not satisfy AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2.
Simple deception involves sending false messages to another person (production of socially relevant information); contrast meets social communication criteria and is a group whole-brain analysis.
The contrast emphasizes inferring others' beliefs and conflict monitoring rather than self-reflection or agency; does not meet PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/I2.
Simple deception engages representation and inference about others' beliefs (rTPJ, ToM); meets perception-of-others criteria with whole-brain group analysis.

Truth vs deception contrasts message-sending behavior and how messages are perceived/acted upon—core social communication processes; group whole-brain analysis in healthy adults.

Determining genuine truth vs deception involves representations of others' beliefs and expectations (ToM) and associated neural markers (rTPJ, habenula relates to social outcome processing); meets perception-of-others criteria and global requirements.

Parametric modulation of incentive to deceive for simple deception examines how social-motivational conflict in an interactive game modulates social-cognitive network engagement; group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults.

The parametric analysis concerns message-sending behavior and how incentives affect social signaling (deception), constituting social communication and is derived from a whole-brain group map in healthy adults.

Modeling incentive to deceive addresses how representations of others' payoffs and expected choices influence neural responses (ToM-related); meets criteria for perception/understanding of others and global requirements.
